title: Tangency, gliding and generalized characteristic motion
reviewed_arguments: A general smooth real symbol with a nondegenerate double normal root is prepared on both signs of the discriminant using the full Morse inverse, even/odd descent, parameter cutoff series and explicit nonzero divided-difference multiplier. The prescribed canonical pair preserves the boundary. Negative units reverse the Hamilton orientation.

All normal contact jets, defining-function changes, the symplectic constraint space and invariant gliding field are calculated. The symbol may have stationary tangential points; no unspoken nonzero tangential differential is imposed.

The generalized-arc definition permits transverse reflection accumulation at glancing. Dini bounds give uniform compressed Lipschitz coordinates and half-Holder normal magnitude; tangential motion is C1.

Strict diffraction has its exact quadratic normal lower bound. Strict gliding uses the full normal-energy cancellation, integral comparison through accumulations and uniform normal/tangential estimates.

The cooperative three-variable comparison is proved by strict first contact and the convergent nonnegative matrix exponential. Exact path lengths give the required time powers; contact of order k yields r=O(t^k), rho=O(t^(k-1)) and tangential error O(t^(k+1)).

Increasing contact forcing gives ordinary continuation; decreasing forcing uses h/e^2 and its zero initial limit to force gliding. Both time directions, initial zero intervals, all finite orders and stationary cases are retained. Whole-common-interval uniqueness follows.

Compressed compactness is proved by dense grids and uniform Lipschitz bounds. Transverse hitting maps, strict energies and higher-contact estimates give the actual limiting derivatives at every point. Ordinary lifts converge on compact sets away from limiting reflections.

Reduced clock sections have the computed symplectic form. Finite transverse clock maps with interior endpoints are smooth injective symplectic maps. A1 proves that all exact wall-hit clock exceptions form a countable union of smooth null hypersurfaces.

A2 proves open-domain measure preservation from compact cutoff substitution and monotone convergence. It applies to the whole reflected map without a factor for the number of itineraries. Normal strips have volume O(epsilon^3); O(epsilon^-1) grids give exceptional outer measure zero.

Dense finite-arc approximation gives local existence for every clock state, while stationary gliding and strict diffraction supply the other cases. Finite endpoints have the compact escape property. The p=rho^2+r example correctly prevents a universal transverse approximation assertion.

The closed-set trajectory theorem retains uniform compact-anchor secant tangency. Full-coordinate interpolations have the stated normal position/momentum, residual, distance and compressed derivative bounds. Strict gliding restarts at zero energy rather than accumulating interpolation errors.

A3 supplies measurable signed normal components, countable exceptional hits, the actual finite-interval bounded majorant and absolute continuity. The limiting integral equations and Taylor chain rule justify the square-root regularization, proving the full G3 derivative rather than only characteristic containment.

The flat-pulse example has exact dyadic moments, all smooth flatness bounds, nonnegative excursions, exact reflection slopes and the complete homogeneous quadratic Hamilton lift. Its alternative gliding solution proves actual nonuniqueness at infinite contact.

All four original solved exercises are unchanged: strict-contact signs and scales, arbitrary higher-contact parity, full nonlinear preparation multiplier, and the compressed Liouville density. The two original diagrams retain all drawing content; a third exact coordinate diagram explains the measure argument.
